title: Bad root output gives bad auxiliary output
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $g:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and let $O$ be either no output or a decision tree querying coordinates in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with leaves labeled by signs. If the output, viewed as a tree allowed to query all coordinates, fails to compute $g$ on the entire Boolean cube whenever it is present, then $O$ is bad for computing $g$ under the empty fixed-coordinate assignment: when present it fails to compute $g$ on inputs matching that assignment, and when absent it is deemed bad by definition.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ is a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
$O$ is an optional decision tree whose available coordinates are all coordinates
The full-cube output is bad, with absence counted as bad
